activity_context.topic_title: Differentiating an Inverse Function at a Point

feedback.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x}$ and the point $P(4,1)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(1,4)$ is$\,${{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(4,1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{x}} \\ {f}^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{4}} \\ {f}^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(4,1)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(1,4)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(4)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{8})} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
